ui.auto.9d8fc6c0b56d.text:
Clamps the final image to the [0, 1] range.

Prevents overshoot artifacts such as bright halos or negative colors.
Recommended for LDR pipelines; optional for HDR depending on tone-mapping.

When not set OptiScaler controls it via upscalers HDR flag

ui.auto.795b823084f5.text:
Ignores small depth differences before edge detection.

Higher values reduce flickering and noise from minor depth changes, but may soften real geometry edges.
Lower values preserve fine detail but can cause unstable or noisy edge detection.

ui.auto.f32a451804f2.text:
Controls how strongly sharpening is reduced across depth edges.

Higher values more aggressively prevent sharpening across object boundaries (reduces halos).
Lower values allow more sharpening to pass across edges (sharper but riskier).

ui.auto.37fc22fb46a2.text: Controls sharpness at high contrast areas.

ui.auto.4bba4c93c95a.text:
Positive values decrease sharpness at high contrast areas.
Negative values increase sharpness at high contrast areas.

ui.auto.ab8a055a34b3.text:
Areas that are more red will have more sharpness applied
Green areas will get reduced sharpness

ui.auto.f671708a5fc2.text:
Maximum amount of sharpness that motion can add or remove.

Negative values reduce sharpening in motion (recommended).
Positive values increase sharpening in motion.

The final adjustment scales with motion and is capped at this value.

ui.auto.34b1d0edf99c.text:
Minimum motion required before motion-based sharpening adjustment begins.

Higher values ignore small movements (more stable).
Lower values react to subtle motion (more sensitive).

ui.auto.e2d1b29d157f.text:
Defines the motion range over which the effect ramps from zero to full strength.

Values above the threshold are mapped into this range.
Larger values make the response smoother and more gradual.
Smaller values make the effect react more quickly and aggressively.

ui.auto.685c3af31da4.text:

1080 / 1.5 = 720

ui.auto.cd4c20f79428.text:

Note that not every game supports every quality preset

1.5x on a 1080p screen means internal resolution of 720p

ui.auto.4b01cf2066f6.text:
Upscales the image internally to a higher output resolution
then downscales it back to your display resolution

Values <1.0 make the upscaler cheaper
Values >1.0 make image sharper at the cost of performance

If greyed out, please check Git Wiki - Unreal Engine tweaks

Target res and total ratio at the bottom (max. total 3.0!)

Less prone to ringing artefacts, but slightly blurrier.

ui.auto.b6d4b021baae.text:
Heavier version of Lanczos2.
Offers the sharpest image, but is the most prone to ringing.
Considered the best along with Kaiser3.

ui.auto.52a26ab1a7ae.text:
Similar to Lanczos2.
Smoother and less prone to artefacts than Lanczos, but slightly blurrier.

ui.auto.093d05889ead.text:

Far less prone to artefacting than Lanczos3, but much heavier on the GPU.
Considered the best along with Lanczos3.

ui.auto.c870da649cf0.text:
Specialised to prevent artifacts.
Eliminates harsh halos for a natural look, but can appear slightly soft.

ui.auto.61e86dafb438.text:
Controls the DXGI Present sync interval, which determines how
the swap chain waits for vertical refresh.

0  = Present immediately, no VSync wait.
1  = Sync to every refresh, normal VSync.
2+ = Present every N refreshes, reducing effective frame rate.

Higher values can reduce tearing but may increase latency and cap FPS.
For most games, use 0 for lowest latency or 1 for normal VSync.
